**`SearchStrategy`** is now a pure `@FunctionalInterface` — one abstract method, no embedded constants. The interface only describes the contract; it no longer contains implementations. This makes it immediately subclassable or mock-able in tests without wading through `BTree`'s internals.

**`SearchStrategies` enum** lives at the top level alongside `BTree` and `Main`. The per-constant abstract method body pattern (`LINEAR { ... }`, `BINARY { ... }`) is the idiomatic Java way to give each enum constant its own behaviour while keeping them type-compatible with the interface. This also means the two strategies are enumerable (`SearchStrategies.values()`), serialisable, and naturally singleton — all without any extra boilerplate.

**`BTree`'s default constructor** changes from `SearchStrategy.LINEAR` to `SearchStrategies.LINEAR` — the only callsite that needed updating.
